findings.title: Add/remove members read group_id but the route only sets id
findings.body: add_members and remove_member load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes are member routes (PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails sets params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The client calls /admin/groups/<id>/members.json and only puts usernames or user_id in the body. require(:group_id) therefore raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove returns 400. destroy and update in this same controller correctly use params[:id]. The controller specs pass group_id straight into the action and never go through the router, so they stay green.

findings.title: Public members page only loads 50 users and cannot page
findings.body: setupController now calls model.findMembers(), which always requests /groups/:name/members.json with the Group model's default limit of 50 and offset 0. The public members template only iterates that one page and has no next/previous or load-more control; paging was added only on the admin group screen. Non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups returned up to 200. A group with more than 50 members now hides the rest with no way to reach them.

findings.title: Creating a group ignores alias_level
findings.body: create only assigns name and visible. The admin form shows the alias-level combo before the group has an id, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups. update applies params[:alias_level], but create never reads it, so a non-default level (for example everyone/99) is not saved. The client keeps the unsaved value until the group is reloaded, so the admin thinks the setting stuck.

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when the count divides the page size
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members, limit 50) that is 2, not 1. showingLast compares currentPage to that value, so the next guard does not fire on the real last page. next then sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count), which equals user_count and loads an empty page. The same formula also leaves the admin on a blank last page after removing the final member of a page, because findMembers keeps the server's unclamped offset.

findings.title: Remove link is shown for automatic groups
findings.body: The remove control is wrapped in {{#unless automatic}} inside the group-member itemView. With {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, Ember sets that view's context to the item view (so {{member}} works) or to the user, not to the admin group. automatic is not the group's automatic flag there; it is missing, so the unless is always true. Automatic groups still show a remove button. The server answers 422, and removeMember has no failure handler, so the admin confirms and the member stays with no error.

findings.title: Add/remove membership failures are silent and the add field is not cleared
findings.body: addMembers posts usernames and on success reloads the current offset, but it never clears usernames (the TODO on the line above). The selector still holds the same names, so another click resubmits them. Neither addMembers nor removeMember handles a rejected promise. A 400, 422, or 500 leaves the list unchanged and shows no alert, which looks the same as a successful add of a user who sorts onto a different page because the reload does not reset offset to 0.

findings.title: Membership specs never hit the router and one uses PUT
findings.body: The automatic-group remove example calls xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is DELETE, and both add_members and remove_member examples pass group_id. Controller specs invoke the action directly, so they pass even though the router only sets params[:id] and the live requests 400. There is also no spec for the public GroupsController#members contract (limit, offset, and the {members, meta} shape) that this PR changes.
